uncited: This method is chosen when rendering requires consistent sampling within a defined spatial partition without blending data from neighboring partitions.
*   **Input:** A 3D sampling position $p$ in world or texture space; a multiresolution volume structure composed of blocks with varying resolutions.
**Index Texture:** A 2D or 3D texture storing metadata for each block.
*   World-space bounding box or origin coordinates.
**Packed Texture:** The actual volumetric data, organized into mipmaps or separate textures per block, storing the scalar values.
**Determine Closest Block:** Identify the block containing or closest to the sampling position $p$.
**Clamp Sampling Position:** Transform $p$ into the local coordinate system of the identified block.
This prevents sampling from invalid or undefined regions at the edges of lower-resolution blocks.
It is chosen when continuity across block boundaries is required, unlike Intrablock which isolates sampling.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per sample, assuming constant-time block lookup and texture sampling.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Depends on the multiresolution hierarchy storage (e.g., octree or brick structure).
*   **When to Use:** When rendering within a single resolution level or when block boundaries are not visually critical; when hardware constraints favor simple, localized lookups.
*   **When Not to Use:** When high visual continuity across varying resolution blocks is required; in such cases, Interblock sampling is preferred.
This method originates from research into GPU-based volume raycasting, specifically in the context of advanced illumination techniques.
